title: Collections Terms — Payment-History Cushion on a Utility Pass-Through Service Final-Statement Prepayment
content:
**Term.** When a prepayment of the estimated final Utility Pass-Through Service statement is quoted, a cushion is added to the estimated final statement: 20 percent of it where a returned payment stands on the lease ledger or on the utility account in the last twelve months, 10 percent of it where neither carries a returned payment in the last twelve months but a late fee stands on the utility account or on the lease ledger in that period, and nothing otherwise; the cushion is rounded half up to the cent. The cushion is added to the prepayment quoted.

**Records read.** The lease ledger is the rent ledger of the Home-Site Lease the account serves; the utility account is the Utility Pass-Through Service account itself. An entry stands in the last twelve months when fewer than 12 whole months separate its date from the handling date. A returned payment is a payment returned unpaid by the bank; a late fee is a late fee charged on that ledger.

## Combinations

| Returned payment in the last 12 months (lease ledger or utility account) | Late fee in the last 12 months (utility account or lease ledger) | Cushion |
|---|---|---|
| Yes, on either | Yes or no | 20 percent of the estimated final statement |
| No, on both | Yes, on either | 10 percent of the estimated final statement |
| No, on both | No, on both | nothing |

## Worked figures (hypothetical estimated final statement of 86.01)

- A returned rent payment on the Home-Site Lease 5 months ago: 20 percent of 86.01 is 17.202, so the cushion is 17.20.
- No returned payment, a utility late fee 8 months ago: 10 percent of 86.01 is 8.601, so the cushion is 8.60.
- A returned utility payment dated exactly 12 whole months before the handling date and nothing else: that entry is not in the last twelve months, so no cushion.
